The mock wrapper itself asserts exactly one matching URL and supplies nonempty should messages. A single string argument at that wrapper call is not a missing assertion message. This test does not launch an OS browser, exercise Enter, prove all reserved-character round trips or validate malformed-percent handling.",
        "Manual comment/style check: the added reason comment names the later encoding step and the parameter re-encoding issue in this field. This is not a global instruction to decode every URL with decodeURIComponent; other multi-URL and mailto consumers have separate contracts. Nearby unrelated assertions are outside the changed scope. No browser, feed fetch, external app, keyboard or accessibility execution occurred.",
        "Read complete retained Bug 1971035 description/comments 0–21, edited comment 14, updates/footer. The reported Website header path changes a percent-encoded comma from %2C to %252C. The separate +security release-link symptom is not assumed to have the same cause. The initial suggestion to stop encoding is superseded by the actual decodeURIComponent display-side change; final UrlHeaderRow still encodes before opening.",

The reviewer requests a test, then corrects the dependency from Bug 1972723 to Bug 1972727. The owned patch adds the direct mocked Website-URL regression assertion. A later reviewer rejects unspecified earlier code with Uhhh, what; the author attributes it to an experimental copy/paste error. The available thread does not show that exact expression, so its contents are not invented. The final assigned patch does not edit header-fields.js, and the accepted current click/Enter consumer still uses encodeURI.",
        "The author's assertion that decodeURIComponent works for complete URIs is a scoped rationale, not a general decoder rule. Source and the fixture directly support the comma round trip for this Website field. The test wrapper checks exactly one dispatched URI and supplies nonempty should messages; this does not establish live external-browser behavior, all reserved-character semantics, malformed input or keyboard results.",

The author identifies Bug 1972727 as a dependency and proposes dropping incompatible test lines; the branch follow-up is reported to drop tests while retaining the code change. Those ESR helper bodies and backport diffs were not read. Daily/Beta verification is an author uplift report; the same form says no automated coverage despite the actual mainline test addition, so the form does not erase the source test evidence. Later tracking flags intentionally keep the follow-up in the uplift queue and are not a new functional-regression result.",

The individual workflow proposal in Bug comment 16 does not change user-directed workflow instructions. No feed URL, screenshot, linked job, OS browser, test, keyboard or accessibility execution was performed."
